about: Every mutant was applied to the file as it is at base_commit, which the change that adds this record does not change: it adds only tests, to the test module of the file's own tests (agent_import_invoice_scope_tests.rs) and to the invoice admission tests (agent_import_invoice_admission_tests.rs), the latter because a listing of ledgers can only be had from that module's lab harness (the extent a listing carries cannot be built by hand). killer is the first test nextest reported failing (it stops at the first failure, with tests running in parallel, so another failing test may be reported first on another run). killer_at says where that test function exists: base, or this_commit for a test the change that adds this record adds. A test that exists at base may still kill only through cases that change adds to it: before_this_change gives the verdict at base where it differs. Each mutant that survived its filtered run at base was run again at base against every bridge test (the whole_set run, with no filter and nextest's --no-fail-fast, the approval stand-in example built) before it was called a survivor. Every survivor left at this_commit is listed in accepted_survivors with its reason: an equivalent one is marked equivalent. A hand-written mutant's mutation id is the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its edits in order, each as its from text, a NUL byte, its to text and a NUL byte, in UTF-8. Each edit's from text occurs exactly once in the file at base_commit, and applied_to names the file it was applied to. A tool mutant is named as cargo-mutants --list names it, by line and column. A mutant whose edit does not compile is recorded as unviable with the compiler's reason, not as caught. The hand-written mutants (S01 to S88) change, one at a time: in from_catalogue, the set of names (not deduplicated or ordered, only the first resolved, resolved in reverse), the exact-name find (case folded, trimmed, the first row that differs, containment), the refusal for a name the catalogue lacks (another code, no ledger named, the name lower-cased), the refusal for a GUID outside the alphabet (another code, no ledger named), the GUID parsed (upper-cased, trimmed), the refusal for a ledger with no usable parent (another code, no ledger named, an Absent parent accepted as empty, an Unsupported parent accepted as empty), the GUID key (kept as spelt, upper-cased), the stored name (empty, lower-cased, trimmed), the stored parent (empty, lower-cased, trimmed, the ledger's name), the GUID put in the part (not at all, twice), and the refusal for an unplannable part (another code, no cause, a ledger rather than a value detail); in parents, the members swapped, the name in place of the parent, the order reversed, only the first, the first left out, the GUID upper-cased, the parent lower-cased; in prove, the count check (<, >, ==), the refusal code and the lack of a cause, the cause of the count refusal, of a row without a GUID, of an unnamed row, of a repeated row and of a differing row, the row's GUID not lower-cased and upper-cased, the repeat check inverted and never firing, the name and parent comparison (|| as &&, each half alone, each half inverted, the name case folded and trimmed, the parent case folded and trimmed, a row with no parent passing), and the loop (the first row not examined, only the first examined, the last not examined); in prove_listing, the refusal code and the lack of a cause, the loop (the first record not examined, only the first examined, the last not examined), the GUID looked up by the lower-cased name, the cause of a record without a GUID, of an unnamed record and of a differing record, the record's GUID not lower-cased and upper-cased, the name and parent comparison (|| as &&, each half alone, each half inverted, the name case folded and trimmed, the parent case folded and trimmed, a parent the listing did not return passing, and returned_text replaced by workbook_text). Not mutated: the derive lists, the visibility of the items, the doc comments, the test module's attribute and path, the body of part (the tool mutates it; it does not compile), the order of the repeat check against the name and parent comparison inside prove, which of two ledgers with the same GUID the map keeps (the catalogue refuses a repeated GUID), the type of the set that detects a repeat, and the wording of the closure that builds a refusal; every edit above is one change, so none of the lists above is every possible change to the line it names. Fifteen edits (S02, S04, S06, S07, S17, S32, S34, S42, S47, S50, S57, S76, S79, S84 and S86) were changed to an equivalent edit of the same kind (a neighbouring spelling of the same change: next() for take(1), str::eq_ignore_ascii_case(row, name) for the method call, !(a == b) for a != b, find(name).is_some() for contains(name), &("") for &"", &*error.code() for error.code(), name.to_string() for name.clone(), the comparison written the other way round or through eq, to_owned() for to_string(), == true on the inverted test, a closure in place of the method path, is_some_and for unwrap_or, and for S76 the wrong cause ledger_scope_row_count_differs after ledger_scope_row_repeated also gave a digit run), because the first spelling gave a mutation id holding a run of eight or more decimal digits, which the privacy scan refuses; S42 and S76 needed a second respelling. In every run the file was byte for byte as at base_commit, checked after each restore (and, for the tool, after the run); the restore was a copy, never a rename. In the tool, hand and whole_set runs the test modules were as at base_commit; in survivors_again they are as this change leaves them.

runs.command: cargo mutants --in-place -p bridge --file src/agent_import_invoice_scope.rs --test-tool nextest --cargo-arg=--locked --timeout 900 --no-shuffle -- -E 'test(/agent_import::invoice::/) | test(/agent_import::tests::invoice_admission_tests::/) | test(/agent_import::post::e2e_tests::/) | test(/agent_import::tests::number_identity_tests::/) | test(/tally::approved_import::/) | test(/invoice/)'

each mutant's edits applied as exact text, then cargo nextest run --locked -p bridge -E 'test(/agent_import::invoice::/) | test(/agent_import::tests::invoice_admission_tests::/) | test(/agent_import::post::e2e_tests::/) | test(/agent_import::tests::number_identity_tests::/) | test(/tally::approved_import::/) | test(/invoice/)'

as the hand run with every bridge test (cargo nextest run --locked -p bridge --no-fail-fast -E 'all()'), for the 20 hand-written mutants the filtered run missed (the tool's run had no mutant missed); the unmutated baseline passed all 4862

as the hand run with -E 'test(/agent_import::invoice::scope::tests::/) | test(/a_listing_row_is_held_to_the_catalogue_at_every_position/) | test(/a_parent_the_listing_did_not_return_is_not_a_group_called_not_observed/)', for the 20 hand-written mutants that survived the whole_set run
